title: Introduce Skein attention window-fusion kernel and rotary handshake for async KV
author: Ava Martins
body:
Summary:
Introduce a new attention kernel variant (Skein) that fuses window-aware attention tiling with a lightweight rotary/rope handshake protocol for async KV warmup. The change includes a scheduler hint path to enable continuous-batching-friendly placement, an opt-in runtime flag, and a safe fallback to the existing attn path.

Motivation:
We see SLO pressure on p50/p95 for medium-sequence workloads (seq_len 512-1536) where current hybrid kernels either overfetch KV pages or fail to amortize kernel launch overhead. Skein aims to: reduce p99 spikes by avoiding redundant KV fetches across nearby windows; expose a rotary handshake so the KV cache can pre-prepare rotary offsets without blocking request hotpaths; and provide a tiled fusion microkernel that keeps FP16 accumulation stable while enabling fused rotary multiplication inside the kernel.

Design highlights:
- New kernel impl: src/runtime/attn/skein_kernel.cu implements a window-fusion kernel that processes overlapping tiles and reuses partial softmax state across adjacent windows. The microkernel integrates rotary multiplication in-register to avoid extra memory traffic.
- Rotary handshake: src/runtime/kv/rotary_handshake.cc/.h provides a small protocol between scheduler and KV cache to publish (rotary_slot, seq_base) metadata so async warmup can apply correct rotary offsets when priming KV shards. This avoids recomputing offsets in the hot path.
- Scheduler integration: src/runtime/scheduler/skein_scheduler.rs adds a placement hint and warmup scorer used by continuous batcher. The batcher will attach a handshake token for requests matching windowed patterns.
- Fallbacks and safety: If the handshake cannot be satisfied (cache miss, incompatible model config), runtime falls back to the current fused_attn path. Added feature-flag `runtime.feature.skein_attn` and a per-model opt-in in the model registry.

Benchmarks (runcards attached):
- Dense transformer (12B, seq=1024, batch=8) on p4d: mean throughput +9.8%, p99 latency -14%, 95th tail improvement -11%.
- Small LLM (1.5B, seq=512, batch=16): throughput +7.2%, p50 latency -6%.
- Memory overhead: ~+2.5% KV cache metadata.
Note: microbench harness under benchmarks/2026/02/skein_{cfg}.json contains warm/cold scenarios used.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests for rotary handshake and kv priming (unit/kv/rotary_handshake_test.cc).
- Kernel-level correctness verified via fp16 and fp32 reference tests (tests/attn/skein_kernel_{fp}.py).
- End-to-end smoke on Dedicated infra pipeline with canary config.

Risks and mitigations:
- Numerical drift: fused rotary-in-register may change fp16 accumulation rounding. Added regression evals in evals/rotary_regression/ to detect semantic deltas for top-5 tokens on standard prompts.
- Cache metadata increased memory: default rollout is disabled for small instances; rollout gating enforced by autoscaler thresholds.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature off in main by default and available behind model opt-in and runtime flag.
2) Enable for internal perf experiments on staging for select models (A/B 10%).
3) Canary on Dedicated GPU pool (5% capacity) with tight alerting on latency/quality regressions.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% then full when no regressions seen for 7 days.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation with CUDA microkernel and tests
- [x] Rotary handshake protocol and unit tests
- [x] Scheduler hint and continuous-batching integration
- [x] Benchmarks and runcards committed
- [x] Docs note in docs/perf/skein-notes.md
- [x] Feature flag and model opt-in

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on kernel correctness (safety for fp16) and handshake atomicity for concurrent warmup races.
- The scheduler changes are intentionally small; they add a scorer and attach a lightweight token. The heavy lifting is in the kernel and KV components.

Related work:
- See ENG-4362 for planning, and SUP-9876 for a support ticket where hotpath tail spikes were observed.

review_comments: Samir Patel (2026-02-18): Left a couple notes around fp16 accumulation — please add a numerics test that compares against the reference kernel for long sequences.
Ava Martins (2026-02-19): Added numerics test and adjusted accumulation path using compensated summation. See tests/attn/skein_kernel_fp16_test.py.
Eleni Korhonen (2026-02-22): Scheduler scorer looks good; please ensure the scorer is cheap (microbench some scorer overhead).
Diego Ramos (2026-02-25): CI showed a flaky CUDA memcheck on sm80, re-ran and added a fence in rotary_handshake to avoid races; stable after rerun.
Samir Patel (2026-02-27): Approving after verifying regression evals on staging.
release_notes: Introduces the Skein attention kernel: a window-fusion attention microkernel with fused rotary handling and an async KV rotary handshake protocol. Provides reduced tail latency for medium-length sequences and an opt-in rollout path.
merge_result: Merged via squash by Eleni Korhonen on 2026-03-01 (squash and merge). Commit message preserved summary and runcard links.
notes: This PR is intentionally opt-in. Operators should watch evals/rotary_regression metrics and the scheduler warmup hit-rate dashboards when enabling.
